name: Vulcan Materials Company
moat_justification: Permitted quarry reserves are close to irreplicable (permitting barriers create local monopolies), transport economics protect each quarry's local radius, and pricing power is proven through the cycle (mix-adjusted price +6% FY2025, +4-5% Q2 2026, cash gross profit per ton rising through an energy shock). Not wide (9-10) because the product is an undifferentiated commodity, volumes are hostage to the construction cycle and public budgets, and returns carry a heavy continuous capex load.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 8.08 vs 3-yr median 5.66 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 3.9x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Strong-moat aggregates compounder (moat 7/10) with proven pricing power, but at $239.33 it prices in far more than even the super-bull case delivers - weighted IRR 6.87%, weighted IV@15% $79.51; clears the 15% hurdle only at or below $79.51.
moat_for: Permitted reserves scarce and effectively irreplicable - permitting barriers create local quarry monopolies
Transport-cost economics: proximity to job site decides the sale; network sits near high-growth metros
Proven pricing power: mix-adjusted price +6% FY2025, +4-5% Q2 2026, cash gross profit per ton rising despite diesel headwind
Scale/density as No. 1 US aggregates producer; public infrastructure demand cushions private downturns
Long reserve life; aggregates-led portfolio after California ready-mix divestiture (June 2026)
moat_against: Undifferentiated commodity product - moat is location/permits, not the product
Cyclical volumes: housing weakness already cut same-store shipments in FY2025; private construction is rate-sensitive
Energy/diesel and labor cost exposure compressed Q2 2026 operating earnings despite price gains
Heavy continuous capex and acquisition dependence to sustain volume growth
Regulatory/environmental regime also constrains Vulcan's own expansions and operations
